Unraveling the Mystery: Paisley Park’s Interactive Tuesday Photo Challenge

Sender: Paisley Park (@PaisleyPark)
Date: October 30, 2018
Time: 17:24 GMT
Subject: Fan identification challenge for a Prince-related photo
Link:

On October 30, 2018, the official Paisley Park account posted a playful interactive challenge as part of its #InteractiveTuesday series. The post asked followers, “Who can tell us what this is a photo of? Check back later to see if you’re right!” accompanied by the hashtags #Prince #PaisleyPark #InteractiveTuesday.

The attached close-up image showed embroidered or printed text on fabric reading “We’re hip dudes we wanna ‘ROCK,’” set against a green-and-white background with cartoon-style lettering. The post generated modest engagement—78 likes, 12 reposts, and 11 replies—as fans offered guesses. One early reply identified it as a detail from the iconic customized denim jacket associated with Prince’s Sign o’ the Times era, a garment known for its safety pins, patches, fringe, and graphic appliqués that became a signature look in the 1987 concert film and live performances.

This lighthearted quiz reflects Paisley Park’s ongoing role as a museum and cultural hub dedicated to preserving Prince’s legacy in Chanhassen, Minnesota. By inviting fans to decode visual artifacts from his wardrobe and creative output, the account fosters community engagement around the musician’s distinctive visual and musical identity long after his passing. https://t.co/JqagOW3Dwh

💥BOOM!!! @KamronRoberts9 EARNS TENNESSEE OFFER.  Love it.  Program Fit Analysis Below⤵️⤵️

Overall Fit
Kamron Roberts projects as a high-upside boundary or nickel corner whose verified 6'5.5" wingspan, twitch, and sticky man-coverage production align precisely with Jim Knowles’ multiple 4-2-5 hybrid scheme that has elevated Tennessee’s pass defense to elite levels in 2026. 

His active hands, efficient hip flip, and ability to erase deep targets while logging high-volume PBUs give the Vols immediate disruption potential in Cover 1 and pattern-match looks that force quarterbacks into hesitation. Roberts’ competitive run support and TFL production add value beyond pure coverage, fitting Knowles’ emphasis on synchronized pressure and secondary toughness that has limited explosive plays to a national minimum. 

As a coachable, multi-sport athlete with a team-first mindset, he accelerates secondary culture in a room transitioning from transfer-heavy seniority toward multi-year internal development. His 4.5 speed and 36" vertical create mismatch advantages on the perimeter or in the slot against SEC receivers, supporting early rotational snaps and special-teams impact while he adds functional mass. 

Early Power Four interest, including the recent Vols offer, validates his trajectory as a Day-1 contributor who develops into a multi-year starter anchoring coverage units. Roberts’ production in competitive high-school settings, roughly 33 tackles, 10+ PBUs, 2 INTs, and 8.0 TFLs signals readiness for the physical, assignment-sound demands of Knowles’ disguised coverages and front variations.

▫️Program Overview
Under head coach Josh Heupel, Tennessee has established offensive consistency while prioritizing defensive reconstruction in 2026. The hiring of Jim Knowles as defensive coordinator brought a hybrid multiple 4-2-5 framework featuring Cover 1, Cover 3 match, Quarters, and 3-high concepts with front variations that disguise pressure and coverage. Knowles’ unit leads the nation in sacks while ranking among the top in pass defense (approximately 159 yards per game) and has allowed the fewest 30-plus-yard pass plays in the SEC. 

Vulnerabilities may center on secondary depth longevity, as several current contributors are seniors or transfers, creating future needs for length, ball skills, and run support that can sustain the scheme without heavy portal reliance. Culture markers emphasize character recruitment, daily work ethic, and leadership that raise standards, as articulated by staff across position groups. Recent performance shows a “suffocating” defense capable of complementary football with Heupel’s offense, with the secondary playing a key role in limiting explosives and supporting the rush.

Roberts’ skill set matches this system through his length and verticality that exploit pattern-match and man principles, active hands for re-routing and finishing plays, and competitive toughness that fills for run support without sacrificing coverage assignment. His film shows clean transitions into trail technique and high-pointing the ball, aligning with Knowles’ requirement for defensive backs who buy time for pressure while remaining sound against vertical and intermediate concepts. The Vols’ emphasis on multi-year development for younger talent makes Roberts’ coachability and production trajectory a direct fit for building internal depth behind current seniors.

▫️Prospect's Fit & Immediate Impact
Roberts aligns primarily as a boundary corner or nickel, with secondary versatility at safety or hybrid packages that leverage his 6'0/175 frame and 6'5.5" wingspan. Day-1 contributions include rotational snaps in man or match looks, special-teams coverage where length and speed disrupt returns, and situational disruption via PBUs and TFLs that complement the front’s sack production. 

His ability to produce in competitive environments evidenced by tight coverage on high-end receivers resulting in incompletions and multiple PBUs supports early ROI while older players rotate or graduate. Growth in off-man and zone footwork consistency will accelerate his path to consistent three-down snaps in Knowles’ varied coverage package. Over three to four seasons, Roberts projects as a high-character leader whose production and daily habits elevate the room, providing scheme-proof coverage traits rare at the 3-star level and reducing reliance on annual portal additions.

▫️Scheme Alignment Breakdown
Knowles’ 2026-27 philosophy prioritizes adaptability across fronts and coverages, using the “Leo” hybrid and disguised safeties to create mismatches while relying on perimeter corners who can play sticky man or pattern-match without false steps. Film of Roberts shows efficient change-of-direction that mirrors vertical routes and closes cushions late, exploiting the scheme’s need for defenders who stay in phase against deep balls while the rush generates pressure. 

His active hand usage at the line for pressing and re-routing transitions cleanly into trail technique, countering SEC offenses that test boundaries with vertical concepts; this matches Knowles’ Cover 1 and match principles where corners must finish with controlled leverage rather than lunging. 

Against high-end receivers, Roberts has produced tight coverage on deep balls ending incomplete plus high-volume PBUs in man looks, directly supporting the Vols’ elite ranking in limiting explosives. Run support with urgency and length to set the edge, combined with 8.0 TFLs, fits the hybrid front’s demand for secondary players who fill assignment-sound without creating seams. 

Current secondary coaches, including co-defensive coordinator/secondary coach Anthony Poindexter and cornerbacks coach Derek Jones, emphasize technique, toughness, and development that align with Roberts’ coachable demeanor and multi-sport discipline. His ball skills—tracking over the shoulder, high-pointing with timing, and finishing plays—enhance pattern-match structures where instincts and length create mismatches. As the defense continues refining timing and disguise under Knowles, Roberts’ physical profile and production provide a developmental piece that accelerates the transition from transfer-heavy seniority to sustainable internal talent.

text:
I finally took the time to analyze $TSLA Q3'26 earnings call. 

While we are all aware of the reasons for why $TSLA won't skyrocket higher from here and instead go lower, there are some arguments to be made on why it could break past resistance and go higher.

First, the Cybercab fleet in Austin has grown by a factor of 10 since launching last month. Tesla has been rapidly deploying CyberCabs in Texas, and eventually, the Tesla team will make the robotaxi business have 24/7 operations and cover more weather/high-speed conditions by the end of the year.

Plus, Elon even noted that they have a clear path to their target of $0.30 per paid mile because they own the vehicle manufacturing and have no driver costs. They'll get there eventually, not now. 

Secondly, Optimus began production in the Fremont factory, and management expects to deliver Optimus to companies outside Tesla around Q4 2027.

A non-pre-programmed, real-world AI demo video is expected in 1-2 months, and that will boost investor confident into Optimus becoming a sales catalyst in the near future. 

In terms of their bread-and-butter automotive business, Elon noted that over 75% of deliveries in North America included a paid FSD subscription, with over 1.7 million paid customers globally, and half of them are on the subscription plan.

Management confirmed investor estimates that FSD Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) is approaching $1 billion.

Unsupervised FSD is expected to roll out in Q2'27, and with that rollout, they'll let customers release their vehicles into the robotaxi network so that owners can get a piece of the profits that are to be made in the growing robotaxi business.

In ways, this move helps them offer lower prices, as many Tesla customers who would put their vehicles into the robotaxi network would happily take any money from servicing a ride rather than let their vehicle bake in the sun. 

Tesla is currently having its highest backlog in 4 years and is doing everything it can to produce more vehicles. The high gas prices have helped a lot with boosting demand for Tesla vehicles, and the price hikes have boosted their automotive gross margins from 16% to 18%. 

By 2030, Tesla hopes to produce 5 million vehicles annually. Factories are already operating at record rates, and Tesla will open more factories in the future.

In terms of energy, Tesla almost sold out of all Megapacks for 2027. The average selling price and margins on Megapacks will grow due to the insane demand for batteries thanks to the AI buildout.

Terrafab, which will be key to Tesla's new chapter, will see its first test chip be produced in May/June 2027, with volume production looking to start in Q3 2028. 

Financially, Tesla is solid with $45B in cash and over $1.5B in FCF during Q3'26. While they revised CapEx spending projections for 2026, next year and the year after will have higher CapEx spending due to the Terafab, robotaxi expansion, Optimus production, and buying more Nvidia GPUs. 

One can argue that robotaxis and a sold-out auto and energy business make for a great bull case for $TSLA. But I think that once they are in the final phases of their CapEx spending and the investments will start bearing fruit, that's when Tesla will truly go on another generational run sometime in 2028. 

Other than that, let's enjoy the opportunity we have in accumulating more shares of an innovative business with a bright future.

🤰🏻🤰🏽🤰🏿 Pregnancy Days 183 to 189 (Week 27): Phase Three: Rhythm and Hiccups
📚 Source: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. To maintain medical accuracy, every lesson is fact-checked by Grok (Sal). General pregnancy education only, not medical advice. Always talk with your doctor or midwife.
🥁 Tap. Tap. Tap. Tap. If you feel a steady little rhythm in your belly this week, your baby may have the hiccups. It is harmless and common. Your baby already lives with rhythm: your heartbeat, your steps, your songs. So what beat will you clap this week?

📌 This week: the last week of the second trimester. You may feel your baby's hiccups as small, rhythmic jerks. Sleep and wake times grow more regular, and the brain is very active. Your baby is about 14 1/2 inches from head to heel and weighs close to 2 pounds, about the size of a head of cabbage.

👶 Where your baby is this week

If conception happened around day 14, your baby is 169 to 175 days old this week. Last week the eyes began to open. This week brings rhythm.

Many mothers start to feel hiccups, small jerks that come in a steady beat for a few minutes. Hiccups are a normal part of how the breathing muscles practice.

Your baby's sleep and wake times are becoming more regular, and the brain is very busy growing. Your baby is about 14 1/2 inches from head to heel and weighs close to 2 pounds.

🤰 Your body this week

This is the end of the second trimester. Many doctors suggest the Tdap vaccine between Weeks 27 and 36, and your visits will soon come every two weeks.

Leg cramps, back pain, heartburn, and shortness of breath are common. Call your doctor or midwife right away for regular tightenings, bleeding, leaking fluid, a severe headache, changes in your vision, sudden swelling, or much less movement than usual.

🎵 Why singing, not talking

Talking needs understanding. Singing is melody, rhythm, and pitch, and those can be received before understanding arrives. Hearing usually begins between about Week 18 and Week 26, and word meaning comes after birth. From conception your baby is a spirit being, and GUP songs go spirit to spirit.

GUP songs are baby music with a purpose: gentle like lullabies, repeating like nursery rhymes, and full of phonic songs the whole family can sing. This is your child's first kids music.

🔤 Phase Three: clap the beats

This week, clap the beats in words. "Ba-by" has two claps. "Hap-py" has two. "Hal-le-lu-jah" has four. Clapping the parts of words is one of the first skills of reading, and you can start it now on the melody.

📖 One song, three ways

Morning: hear the Week-27 song and thank God for your baby's rhythm. Midday: hum it with headphones on, then clap the beats of your baby's name. Evening: write each word with its beats marked on your Word List page.

👨 Dad, headphones on you too. Clap the beat while she sings.

🙏 Pray and remember

📖 “All nations, clap your hands. Shout joyfully to God with a voice of exultation.” (Psalm 47:1; CPDV 46:2)

🎂 “Muhammad Ali was born January 17, 1942. He boxed with a dancer's rhythm and made up rhyming poems about his fights, and he became a three-time heavyweight champion of the world.”

🙏 "Father God, thank You for the rhythm of our baby's life. Let every beat of our child's heart praise You. In Jesus' name, amen."

✅ Prenatal vitamin every day. Asked about Tdap. Heard, hummed, and wrote this week's song. Clapped the beats. Dad clapped along. Next week: Welcome to the Third Trimester.

🔎 Pregnancy Deep Dive: Week 27 (Days 183 to 189): Phase Three: Rhythm and Hiccups

🗓 Week 27 at a Glance

Week 27 is pregnancy days 183 to 189, counted from the first day of your last period, the count used by doctors, midwives, and pregnancy calculators. If conception happened around day 14, your baby is between 169 and 175 days old. In longer or shorter cycles, these days shift a little.

This is the last week of the second trimester, and it is a week of rhythm. Many mothers start to feel hiccups. Sleep and wake times are becoming more regular. The brain is very active, the lungs keep maturing, and your baby keeps adding fat.

Your baby is about 14 1/2 inches from head to heel and weighs close to 2 pounds, about the size of a head of cabbage. Next week the third trimester begins.

🗓️ The Week, Day by Day

Here is the week counted in days after conception. In a 28-day cycle, add 14 to find your pregnancy day. Babies grow at their own pace, so use this as a guide.

Days 169 and 170 (pregnancy days 183 and 184): Your baby may have hiccups, felt as small rhythmic jerks that last a few minutes.

Days 171 and 172 (days 185 and 186): Times of sleep and times of activity are becoming more regular.

Day 173 (day 187): The brain is very active, growing and forming new connections.

Day 174 (day 188): The lungs keep adding air sacs and surfactant, though they are still not ready to breathe air.

Day 175 (day 189): Your baby weighs close to 2 pounds and is about 14 1/2 inches from head to heel.

🫧 Hiccups in the Womb

Many mothers notice a steady tapping or jerking in one spot of the belly, coming every few seconds for several minutes. That is often your baby having hiccups.

Hiccups happen when the diaphragm, the main breathing muscle, tightens suddenly. In the womb, hiccups are common and harmless. Many experts think they are part of how the breathing muscles practice and how the nerves that control breathing mature.

Your baby is not uncomfortable. Hiccups may happen several times a day or only now and then. Every baby is different. You may feel them more as your baby grows. If you ever notice a sudden big change in your baby's movement or hiccups late in pregnancy that worries you, call your doctor.

🥁 A Life Full of Rhythm

Your baby lives inside rhythm. Your heartbeat thumps steadily. Your breathing moves in and out. Your steps rock your baby as you walk. Day and night come and go.

Rhythm is one of the earliest things a baby can take in, because it does not need words. That is part of why lullabies and nursery rhymes work so well. They have a steady beat, simple rhyme, and repetition. Babies after birth often calm to a steady rocking rhythm and a gentle song.

The GUP songs you sing each week are full of rhythm. As hearing grows clearer, your baby is living with those rhythms every day. They are becoming as familiar as your heartbeat.

😴 Sleep and Wake

Your baby now has clearer periods of sleep and periods of activity. Some sleep is quiet sleep, with little movement. Some is active sleep, with eye movements, twitches, and small kicks. Awake times bring bigger stretches and rolls.

You may start to notice a pattern. Many babies are busy in the evening or when you lie down to rest. Pay attention this week, and write down when your baby is most active. Starting around Week 28, many doctors ask mothers to pay close attention to their baby's movements each day. Knowing your baby's normal pattern will help.

Sleep for you matters too. Rest when you can. God made both mother and child to need rest.

📖 “In peace itself, I will sleep and I will rest. For you, O Lord, have established me singularly in hope.” (Psalm 4:8; CPDV 4:9)

🎂 “Johnny Cash was born February 26, 1932. He grew up singing hymns with his mother while working the cotton fields in Arkansas, and his steady "boom-chicka-boom" rhythm became one of the most famous sounds in country music.”

🧠 A Busy Brain

Your baby's brain is very active now. Brain cells keep forming connections, and the surface keeps folding to make room. Brain wave studies show more organized activity in this stage, especially during sleep.

The brain will keep growing fast through the third trimester and the first years of life. Everything your child will one day learn, including the words you are singing now, will be stored in this growing brain.

Feed it well: keep taking your prenatal vitamin, eat good fats from low-mercury fish, and get enough rest. And keep singing. Your songs are part of the world your baby's brain is growing in.

👏 Phase Three: Clap the Beats

Phase Three has given you family words, food words, face words, sound words, praise words, and light words. This week you add rhythm to the words. You will clap the beats, called syllables, in each word.

Here is how. Say a word slowly and clap once for each part. "Mom" has one clap. "Ba-by" has two. "Hap-py" has two. "Je-sus" has two. "Hal-le-lu-jah" has four. Now sing the word on the melody of the weekly song and clap as you sing.

Hearing the beats in words is one of the first steps toward reading. Teachers call it hearing syllables. Children who can clap the parts of words have an easier time sounding them out later. You are starting that skill now, months before birth, and you will keep it going after birth with every song you clap together.

Clap your baby's name if you have chosen one. Clap the names of everyone in the family. These clapping songs are phonic songs, nursery rhymes, and kids music rolled into one. They are baby music with a beat.

📖 “Write the vision and explain it on tablets.” (Habakkuk 2:2, CPDV)

🎂 “Dwight D. Eisenhower was born October 14, 1890. He led the careful planning of the D-Day landings in 1944 and later served two terms as president of the United States.”

🗓️ The End of the Second Trimester

This is the last week of the second trimester. Look back at how far you have come since Week 14: the first flutters, the anatomy scan, the halfway mark, the first kicks you could really feel, hearing waking up, the eyes beginning to open.

Look ahead too. The third trimester brings rapid growth, more frequent visits, and the slow preparation for birth. Your baby will add most of the birth weight in these last 13 weeks. The lungs, brain, and fat stores will all grow.

Take a moment this week to give thanks. Write in your journal what you are most grateful for from the second trimester. Then write one prayer for the season ahead.

💃 Moving With Joy

When Mary greeted Elizabeth, the baby in Elizabeth's womb leaped for joy. Movement and joy go together in the Bible. David danced before the Lord. The psalms call people to clap and shout for joy.

This week, let your body move with the music. Sway as you sing. Rock side to side on a chair or a birthing ball. Walk to the beat of the weekly song. Your baby feels your movement and your rhythm. You are dancing together.

📖 “For behold, as the voice of your greeting came to my ears, the infant in my womb leaped for joy.” (Luke 1:44, CPDV)

🎂 “Gene Kelly was born August 23, 1912. His joyful tap dancing through puddles in the 1952 film Singin' in the Rain made it one of the most loved dance scenes ever filmed.”

🤰 Your Body at Twenty-Seven Weeks

Your womb now reaches about halfway between your belly button and your breastbone, and it is growing every week. You may feel heavier, slower, and more tired than a few weeks ago.

Leg cramps at night, back pain, heartburn, swelling, and shortness of breath are all common now. Some mothers notice their hands or feet feel puffy, or their rings get tight. Remove rings if they start to feel snug.

Many women gain about a pound a week from here on, though your doctor will tell you what is right for you. Keep eating well, staying active as your doctor allows, and resting.

💉 Tdap and Your Next Visits

Doctors recommend the Tdap vaccine during every pregnancy, usually between Weeks 27 and 36. It helps protect your newborn from whooping cough, which can be very dangerous for babies too young for their own shots. Family members who will be around the baby can ask their own doctors about being up to date too.

From about Week 28, prenatal visits usually come every two weeks, then every week near the end. If your blood is Rh-negative, your doctor will usually give the Rh shot around Week 28.

Ask your doctor at your next visit about the Tdap timing, your Rh status, and how to pay attention to your baby's daily movements starting next week.

🍼 Thinking About Feeding

Now is a good time to think about how you will feed your baby. Breast milk is made for babies. It carries antibodies, it changes as your baby grows, and doctors recommend breastfeeding when it is possible. If breastfeeding is not possible or not your choice, formula is a safe and healthy way to feed a baby.

If you plan to breastfeed, take a class before birth, ask if your hospital has a lactation consultant, and talk with friends who have nursed. The first days can be hard, and help makes a big difference.

Whatever you choose, feeding time will be one of your best singing times. Your baby will be in your arms, at just the distance where newborns see best, listening to your voice.

🏠 Help After Birth

The weeks after birth are a big change. You will be healing, feeding often, and sleeping little. Now is the time to line up help.

Ask family and friends who can bring meals, run errands, or watch older children. Many churches organize meal trains for new families. Write a list of people to call and what each can do. Talk with Dad about how you will share the night feedings and the housework.

Accepting help is not a weakness. It is how God designed families and churches to carry one another.

🗓️ Planning Time Off

Now is a good time to plan your time away from work after birth, if you work outside the home. Talk with your employer about your leave, when you expect to stop working, and what forms you need. Ask Dad to find out what time off his work offers too.

Think about how you will share the first weeks at home. Who will be with you? Who will help with older children, meals, and errands? Write your plan in your journal.

Plans can change if your baby comes early or if you need extra rest before birth. Build in some flexibility. God directs the steps, even the ones on the calendar.

🦶 A Practice Movement Count

Next week, many doctors begin asking mothers to pay close attention to their baby's movements each day. This week, try a practice run.

Pick a time when your baby is usually active, often after a meal or in the evening. Lie on your side or sit comfortably. Notice each kick, roll, jab, or flutter. Write down the time you start and the time you feel the tenth movement. Do this once a day for a few days.

You will start to see your baby's pattern. Some babies reach ten movements in a few minutes. Others take longer. What matters most is knowing your own baby's normal, so you will notice if it changes. Ask your doctor at your next visit how they want you to track movements.

🌡️ Staying Cool

Pregnancy raises your body's resting temperature and increases your blood flow, so many mothers feel warm all the time, especially in the third trimester.

Dress in light layers you can take off. Use fans and keep your bedroom cool at night. Drink plenty of water, especially in hot weather. Avoid exercising in heat, and rest in the shade or indoors on hot days. A cool shower or a cool cloth on your neck can help.

Call your doctor if you feel faint, confused, very dizzy, or have a fever. Getting too hot can be harmful in pregnancy, so take heat seriously.

💬 Telling Your Doctor About Fears

Many mothers have fears they do not say out loud: fear of labor pain, fear of something going wrong, fear of not being a good mother, fear from a past hard birth or loss.

Your doctor or midwife has heard these fears many times. Tell them. They can explain what to expect, talk through pain relief options, and help you make a plan. If a past birth was very hard, ask whether you can talk with someone about it.

Fear grows in silence and shrinks when it is shared. Write your fears in your journal, pray over them, and bring them to your next visit.

🥜 Snacks That Help

Small, healthy snacks can keep your energy steady, ease heartburn, and help with nausea that sometimes returns late in pregnancy. Good choices include yogurt, cheese with whole-grain crackers, an apple with peanut butter, a handful of nuts, hummus with vegetables, a hard-boiled egg, or a smoothie made with milk and fruit.

Keep snacks in your bag, your car, and by your bed. Eating a little every few hours is often easier than three big meals now that your stomach has less room.

🤝 Prayer Partners

Ask one or two trusted friends, perhaps from church, to be your prayer partners for the rest of your pregnancy. Share your requests each week: your baby's growth, your health, your fears, and the birth. Let them pray with you in person or by phone.

After birth, keep these friendships close. The first months with a baby can feel lonely. Prayer partners can check on you, encourage you, and remind you that you are not alone.

🎼 Rhythm in Daily Life

Your home is full of rhythms: waking and sleeping, meals, work, prayer, and rest. Babies thrive on gentle, predictable rhythms. Start shaping your family's rhythm now. Sing the weekly song at the same times each day. Pray at the same time each night. After birth, these steady patterns will help your baby feel safe and help you find your way through the newborn days.

🎵 Clapping Games for Later

Many old clapping games and rhymes, like "Pat-a-Cake," have been played with babies for centuries. Learn one or two now. After birth, you can gently clap your baby's hands together as you sing. These games teach rhythm, coordination, and the joy of playing together, and they are some of the simplest lessons in God's Home Schooling. Clapping games are kids music at its simplest.

🥗 Body: Caring for the Home This Week

This week, keep your meals steady and your fluids up. Eat three meals and a couple of healthy snacks so you do not get too hungry. Include protein, whole grains, fruits, vegetables, and calcium foods. Drink water often, since dehydration can make cramps and tightenings worse.

Stick with safe food habits. Cook meats, chicken, eggs, and seafood thoroughly. Wash fruits and vegetables. Choose pasteurized milk and cheese. Heat deli meats and hot dogs until steaming hot. Pick low-mercury fish, and steer clear of shark, swordfish, king mackerel, and tilefish.

No amount of alcohol has been proven safe in pregnancy. Avoid all smoking and vaping, including secondhand smoke. Keep caffeine under 200 mg a day. Check with your doctor before any medicine, herb, or supplement, and keep moving gently if your doctor approves.

🚨 Signs to Call About Now

Call your doctor or midwife right away for regular tightenings or cramps, a low backache that comes and goes, pressure in the pelvis, bleeding, or fluid leaking or gushing from the vagina. These can be signs of preterm labor.

Also call right away for a severe headache, vision changes, sudden swelling of the face or hands, pain high on the right side of the belly, a fever, or a big drop in your baby's movement.

If you cannot reach your doctor and something seems serious, go to the hospital. It is always right to be checked.

👨 For Dad: Keep the Beat

Dad, this week is about rhythm, and you can be the drummer. While she sings the weekly song, clap the beat. Then clap the syllables of your baby's name and every family name. Make it fun. Let her laugh.

Pay attention to her body too. Rub her calves when they cramp. Help her up from the couch. Take over tasks that need bending and lifting.

Put your hand on her belly when the baby has hiccups. Feel the little rhythm together. Pray for your baby's growing lungs and brain.

👵 For Grandparents and Siblings

Big brothers and sisters are great clappers. Let them clap the beats in their own names, then in the baby's name. Make a clapping game with the weekly song: one clap for each beat.

Grandparents can teach a clapping rhyme or song from their own childhood. Write it in the journal. Clapping games are some of the oldest nursery rhymes in the world.

🎶 One Song, Three Ways: Week 27

Every week has one GUP song, learned three different ways. A good preschool teacher never teaches an important lesson only once. Teach it three ways, and it is remembered.

Hear it. In the morning, listen once with your eyes closed. Thank God for the rhythm of your baby's life.

Hum it. At midday, put on headphones and hum along. Then clap the beat as you sing, and clap the parts of your baby's name.

Write it. In the evening, listen with your Pregnancy Journal open. Write the phonograms you hear, build a word, and mark its beats with a small line between each part.

GUP songs are baby music with a purpose: gentle like lullabies, repeating like nursery rhymes, and full of the phonic songs that become the building blocks of reading.

📓 Your Pregnancy Journal: Week-27 Pages

On your Word List page, go back over your words and mark the beats in each one, like "ba-by" and "hap-py."

On a "Movement Pattern" page, write when your baby is most active this week, and when you feel hiccups. This will help you next week, when daily movement becomes more important to watch.

On a "Second Trimester" page, write what you are most thankful for from Weeks 14 to 27. Add your Tdap plan and a prayer for the third trimester.

🧭 God's GPS

Some babies come earlier than planned. Some mothers are told to rest more than they hoped. Some pregnancies go just as expected. You cannot see the whole road from here.

But God can. He directs the steps of every mother and every child. Whatever the third trimester brings, He is already there.

📖 “The heart of man disposes his way. But it is for the Lord to direct his steps.” (Proverbs 16:9, CPDV)

🎂 “Wilma Rudolph was born June 23, 1940. Born early and very small, she wore a brace on her leg as a child after polio, yet she won three Olympic gold medals in running in 1960.”

🙏 A Prayer for Week 27

"Father God, thank You for bringing us to the end of the second trimester. Thank You for hiccups and kicks, for sleep and wake, and for a brain growing so fast.

Let the rhythm of our home be the rhythm of praise. Let our child sleep in peace and rest in hope. As we clap the beats of words, build in our baby a love for words, for reading, and for Your Word. Direct our steps into the third trimester. In Jesus' name, amen."

❓ Questions Parents Ask

Are hiccups in the womb normal? Yes. Hiccups are common and harmless. They are part of how the breathing muscles practice.

Should I start counting kicks? Many doctors ask mothers to pay close attention to movement starting around Week 28. Ask your doctor how they want you to do it.

When is the third trimester? Many doctors count the third trimester from Week 28 to birth. This week is the last week of the second trimester.

Why clap syllables now? Hearing the beats in words is an early reading skill. Starting the clapping habit now makes it a natural part of your family's songs after birth.

When do I call my doctor right away? Call for bleeding, leaking fluid, regular tightenings, pelvic pressure, a severe headache, vision changes, sudden swelling of the face or hands, a fever, or much less movement than usual.

✅ Your Week-27 Checklist

I took my prenatal vitamin every day. I drank plenty of water and ate steady meals. I asked about Tdap and the Rh shot. I wrote down my baby's movement pattern.

I heard, hummed, and wrote this week's one song every day. I clapped the beats of words. I marked the beats on my Word List. Dad clapped along. The family played a clapping game.

📚 Source: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. To maintain medical accuracy, every lesson is fact-checked by Grok (Sal). General pregnancy education only, not medical advice. Always talk with your doctor or midwife.

How The Islamic colonization of Africa messed up the indigenous agriculture:

Islamic colonization of the indigenous agriculture introduced the lunar calendar, which are not based on the seasons, is free of the predictability and obligations of the farming cycle. According to Lamin Sanneh, the prescribed Muslim prayer on regular pattern with its anti-agricultural bias unsettled the agricultural scene in indigenous Africa. According to Lamin Sanneh, the “old ritual, tied to the solar, agricultural system, are wrenched from their temporal moorings and allowed to float with no fixed footing in the new lunar cycle. These old rituals then have to bid on terms set by the new religious order, and if they survive, they do so with a fresh orientation. For instance, the harvest essential as the rite of firstfruits, based on the farming calendar, might in that form survive into the Islamic system, but its content is now filled with observance governed by the Muslim ritual code. In the case of the rite of firstfruits, the rules of zakat, of the obligatory tithe, would apply. For example, my mother and other women relatives set apart a fortieth part of the rice harvest as JAKKO, Manding for zakat. In time the JAKKO was completely separated from the old than offering rite over which women presided in the name of the community and became instead an individual assessment on personal produce. It was paid to the IMAM, who might offer a short extempore prayer of thanks in return. … In some case of a severe drought that I can remember, for instance, the women were caught between paying out Jaakko and starving their children on the one hand, withholding it to feed their families., though in so doing they would be violating the norms of jakko. With grim resolve, they decided to pay it out rather than risk the curse of a breach…. “ (Lamin Sanneh, p, 34).

“I am not challenging the mandate because I support it. If it is my job to ensure the health, safety and welfare of the residents of this state, then I think everyone ought to get vaccinated unless they have a medical reason that prevents them from doing so.”

Dana Michelle Nessel holds a B.A. in political science from the University of Michigan (1990) and a J.D. from Wayne State University Law School (1994). She is a former assistant prosecutor in Wayne County for eleven years, private civil-rights and criminal-defense attorney, and Attorney General of Michigan since January 2019. No M.D., no epidemiology, no immunology, no public-health degree, no clinic. The credential for declaring that everyone medically eligible ought to get the shot, and for offering herself as a dunk-tank prize for those who do, is a law degree and the attorney general’s office.

In June 2021 she sat in a dunk tank at a Genesee County expungement fair in Flint. Vaccines were available on site; she tweeted that getting vaccinated earned the right to dunk the AG. In December 2021 she said she would support President Biden’s OSHA vaccine-or-test mandate for large employers before the Supreme Court, that she was not challenging it because she supported it, and that if her job was to ensure the health, safety, and welfare of the state then everyone ought to get vaccinated unless a medical reason prevented them. She said she did not think the United States would have had Delta or Omicron if more people had gotten vaccinated when the shots were available. She called the attorneys general who were challenging the mandate “irresponsible and reckless.” The platform was the attorney general’s office and a county fair. 

She offered a carnival dunk as the incentive, then told the state that the fastest track to normalcy was immediate vaccination for everyone medically eligible, and that the variants themselves were the result of too few people taking the shot. The product did not stop infection or transmission. She is still Attorney General. The workers who faced the large-employer rule she said she would defend in court, and the residents who dunked her after rolling up a sleeve, did not get a correction when the welfare she assigned to the needle failed the one job she assigned it.

She said her job was to ensure the welfare. Then the welfare kept getting infected, and the support for mandates crippled public trust.

THERE - - IT IS.....REALITY CHECK !!  😲

What Does ‘Free’ Democratic Socialism REALLY Cost?
by Les Rubin                October 27, 2026

The promise of government-provided healthcare and other liberal social programs without premiums, deductibles, or copays has a powerful appeal. However, rabidly malignant liberal politicians promoting Democratic Socialism rarely answer a key question: What will it actually cost, and how will we pay for it?

To understand what these promises mean for middle-income families, we need to look beyond the sales pitch and examine the REAL, FACTUAL numbers.

Muslim Democratic nominee for the Senate in Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed, recently said about universal healthcare that “it is guaranteed health insurance from cradle to the moment you pass away. It comes without premiums or co-pays or deductibles.  It guarantees you care when you need it. This is a level of security we have never known in the United States.”

Any country that has adopted some version of national healthcare proves it does NOT work as the advocates "promise". They are paid for through substantial taxes;" there are fees and co-pays required for service, and long waits for many of the medical procedures.

What does it cost and how will it be paid? Advocates argue that "taxing the rich" can pay for these programs. However, studies have repeatedly shown that the additional revenue from taxing high-income earners would fall far short of covering the costs. Even substantially higher taxes on the wealthy cannot close a funding gap of this magnitude, leaving middle- and lower-income taxpayers to shoulder much of the burden.

Sweden provides a useful example. Its tax structure includes a 32 percent tax on wages to fund pensions and other programs, a minimum income tax rate of approximately 32 percent, and a rate of 52 percent on income above $62,000. In addition, Sweden has a value-added tax that averages 19 percent on consumption, along with gasoline taxes that are $2.70 per gallon higher than those in the United States. These taxes are essential to fund the programs that politicians often/falsely hold up as......“free.”

For the $70,000 employee in Sweden, an employer pays $17,000 in pension and other taxes. The employee pays about $17,000 in income taxes on wages. Value-added tax would add $6,500, plus an additional $1,350 in gasoline taxes, compared with what Americans pay. That brings the total tax to $41,850.

For the same employee in the United States, Social Security taxes would be about $8,000, Medicare taxes about $1,800, and medical insurance $1,000, assuming the employer provides it. Income taxes on wages would add about $3,500, and state sales taxes would add $3,900. That brings the total to $18,200.

Based on this comparison, if we wanted the same programs Sweden offers, we would need a tax structure that raises comparable revenue; that would mean paying an additional $23,650 in taxes.

The United States is NOT paying for the programs it already has. For 2026, the gross domestic product was $32.4 trillion.  Expenses were $7.4 trillion, and revenue was $5.4 trillion, leaving a $2 trillion deficit. Covering current expenses would require a 37 percent tax increase or a 27 percent spending cut. According to a Cato Institute study, adding Democratic Socialist programs would add at least $7 trillion to expenses, and tax revenue would need to RISE to 266 percent of current levels.

Economies grow fastest, and the standard of living improves much more rapidly when the government is limited, and taxes cover the cost of government. Adding “free” programs will cause the government to increase dramatically and will slow growth remarkably. This is a fact that is proven repeatedly in the REAL world, NOT a Liberal DEMOCRAT......"theory".

There is nothing inherently wrong with choosing a different model of government, as Sweden has done. That choice has real financial consequences, and middle-income families deserve to know them. Then we can make an intelligent choice.

Before embracing the promise of Liberal Democratic Socialism, voters should ask whether these benefits are worth the added cost, and whether we’re prepared to pay for them. Americans should make that decision with their eyes open, not based on empty promises that gloss over the important facts about cost and how to pay for them.

Remember, there is no "free lunch", so quit......looking for it.

text:
The Sign on the Beach
Diary Log 699SS…1:00am, 30th October 2026. 
Somewhere on the Spanish coast, a cove nobody's claimed.

We found it. A little cove not far from where we were, tucked behind a headland, no car park, no café, no sign pointing to it. Just sand and shingle and the sound of the sea. That's the plan. That's always the plan.

Gobbolino's keeping his distance, as always. He doesn't do water. He sits up on the rocks at the edge of the beach, watching the tide like it's a thing he's decided not to trust. Dave's already in the shallows, sniffing at the foam like it owes him a few bob.

And we're walking, and we come across this thing half-buried in the sand at the back of the beach.
A rusty sign. Old. Weathered. Up on a post, the kind of thing that's been there a while and been ignored for longer.
It says:

ORDINARY HUMAN ACTIVITIES NOW REQUIRE GOVERNMENT PERMISSION.

And then, in columns underneath:

Build on your land. Live in a tiny home. Sleep in public. Feed people. Grow food. Raise animals. Sell what you produce.
Offer your skills. Run a business. Collect rainwater. Handle your own waste. Park a RV. Modify your property.

And at the bottom:

AT WHAT POINT DID MEETING OUR OWN BASIC NEEDS BECOME SOMETHING THAT REQUIRES AUTHORISATION?

May 2020, it's dated. Put up at the beginning of the lockdowns.
I stood there in the dark, and I read it again. And again.
Because here's the thing about that sign. At the time it went up, most people read it as a joke. A bit of dark humour from someone with too much time on their hands. A prediction, maybe, if you were the worrying kind.

But I'm standing here, six years on, and I can't find the joke.
Build on your land. Try it. See how many forms, how many inspectors, how many years of appeals you get through before a single brick.

Live in a tiny home. Try it. Try to park a van, a cabin, a shed on your own ground and see how long before someone official arrives to tell you it's not allowed.

Feed people. Try it. Try to give a meal to someone who's hungry and see how quickly it becomes a licensing issue, a hygiene inspection, a "you can't do that here."

Grow food. Raise animals. Sell what you produce. All of it. All of it now sits behind a wall of paperwork and permits and people whose entire job is to say no.

Collect rainwater. That's the one that gets me. Collecting the rain that falls on your own roof. That's not a privilege. That's not even a right. That's just... a thing a person does. And now it's a form.

Handle your own waste. Park a RV. Modify your property. The list goes on. Every one of them a thing my grandfather would have done without asking anyone.

And the question at the bottom…at what point did meeting our own basic needs become something that requires authorisation?
That's the whole thing, isn't it. That's the whole mechanism in one sentence.

Because it's not a question about rules. It's a question about who you are. At what point did you stop being a person who can do things, and start being a person who must ask permission to do them?

The answer, I think, is this: the moment you accepted that the permission was necessary. That's when you became the kind of person who needs it. That's the real transformation. Not the law. The acceptance.

Dave looks up at me, sand on his nose, and gives a low harrumph. Yeah, he says. That's the one.
Gobbolino's still up on the rocks, watching the tide. He doesn't need to read the sign. He’s been on it since I got him in 2014.

I look out at the water, and I think: the sign was dated May 2020. It was meant as a joke, or a warning.

Six years later, it's a documentary.

The Three Travellers 🐾

text:
His grandma ran a daycare in Texas, and every Thursday she loaded the kids up and took them to a roller rink.

He would race the other kids for candy.

The man who owned the rink kept watching this one little boy finish so far ahead of everybody else that he finally pulled the grandmother aside and told her to go sign him up for real races.

He was five years old. He joined a team over in Arlington, and he had been on wheels since he was two.

By nine he had won his first national championship. He won four of them.

He set national records too. One of them came at the 2017 national championships in Lincoln, Nebraska.

That kid is Keith Abney II, and he is a rookie cornerback for the Detroit Lions.

Right now, nobody who plays his position and entered the league this year has been better. Opposing quarterbacks have a 26.0 passer rating when they throw at him. That is the lowest mark of any rookie corner in football.

He raced until he was about 15 and he was trying to make the United States junior world team.

Here is how he describes those years.

"I was winning races, setting records, all across the country."

Then the pandemic shut the rinks down, and he put it all away and went all in on football instead.

He says the racing is most of why he can cover people.

"Definitely a lot of things translate."

The endurance. The core strength. The ankles, especially, from all those years of holding an edge in a turn at speed.

He also claims to be dangerous at one other thing.

"I can bowl. I'm real good at bowling."

He went to Waxahachie High School, south of Dallas, and he was a three star recruit nobody fought over. He committed to Utah State. Then Arizona State offered late and he flipped on signing day.

He was second team All-Big 12 as a sophomore. By his last year there he was first team All-Big 12. Quarterbacks threw at him 72 times that season, completed 44 percent of them, and did not get a single touchdown.

Be straight about it. He is a rookie and this is a handful of games. Dane Brugler of The Athletic had a second or third round grade on him and 156 players still went before Detroit took him, which usually means the people who do this for a living saw something. Rookie corners get found out in December.

But think about where this started.

He does not race anymore. Here is what he says about that.

"I haven't put on skates in a minute."

He used to beat everybody in the building for candy.

Now he does it for a living.

text:
With respect and deference…No. 

Your president voluntarily surrendered Ukraine’s nuclear arsenal. Nobody forced him to do so, despite his government’s dangerously misplaced confidence in Russia. And for the record, the principal signatories to the Budapest Memorandum were Ukraine, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Russia.

Your president fundamentally misunderstood the distinction between diplomatic assurances and legally binding security guarantees under the American constitutional system. In the United States, treaties generally require the advice and consent of two-thirds of the Senate. The Budapest Memorandum never received that approval.

It was called a Memorandum, not a mutual-defense treaty, for a reason. It established security assurances and political commitments, not an American military obligation to defend Ukraine. No subsequent 

American president inherited a Senate-ratified commitment to send U.S. forces to Ukraine under that document.

And even when Washington makes promises, ask the Kurds and Cubans how reliable American commitments have always been.

Had Ukraine’s leadership been less constrained by the Soviet-era mentality of deference to Moscow, less susceptible to authoritarian influence, and less compromised by corruption, perhaps it would have recognized the catastrophic danger of relinquishing its nuclear deterrent.

Especially when your neighbor is a barbaric Russian regime with a long history of imperial aggression, repression, and territorial conquest.

But let me make something absolutely clear: Do not blame ordinary American citizens for the decisions of American presidents. A substantial majority of Americans have supported Ukraine, and many of us have consistently opposed the appeasement of Vladimir Putin.

We did not all want to give Donald Trump another chance. Many of us recognized him for precisely what he has repeatedly demonstrated himself to be: a narcissistic, racist, authoritarian-minded convicted felon, found liable for sexual abuse, whose conduct has repeatedly disgraced the office of the presidency.

And should President Zelenskyy ultimately surrender territory, sovereignty, or other concessions in exchange for peace, you cannot simply transfer responsibility for those decisions to American citizens.

Trump is not the president of Ukraine. Neither is the British prime minister, the French president, the German chancellor, nor any other Western leader.

They may exert pressure, offer assistance, negotiate, or withhold support. But none of them possesses the democratic mandate to speak for the Ukrainian people or determine Ukraine’s sovereign future.

That responsibility belongs to Ukraine’s elected leadership, accountable to the Ukrainian people.

Ukraine's sovereignty belongs to Ukrainians. America's government belongs to Americans. And neither nation should confuse the decisions of its political leadership with the collective will of every citizen.

Accountability must be directed where it belongs—not indiscriminately assigned to entire populations.

text:
🇺🇦 Ukraine has temporarily halted its long-range strikes on Russian oil refineries, one of its most effective operations against Moscow, after complaints from President Trump, The Wall Street Journal reports

The paper cites people with knowledge of the operations. They say Ukrainian long-range strike units were told in mid-October to put the refinery campaign effectively on hold once missions already in motion were completed. The pause is unofficial and is expected to last until after the US midterm elections on 3 November, possibly longer. Reuters said it could not immediately verify it. Kyiv has not confirmed or denied it on the record.

The public record is consistent with the report. The last Russian refinery strike we can confirm was at Rosneft's Ryazan plant on 15 October. Governor Pavel Malkov reported a fire on site, and the Russian Defense Ministry said it downed 69 drones and 4 Flamingo missiles over the facility. Since then, Ukrainian strikes have hit other targets. On 20 October, Tambov's governor reported a fire that independent monitors linked to a Druzhba pipeline station. On 26 October, Fire Point said its FP-1 drones struck a synthetic rubber plant in Voronezh. Drones also reached Omsk's industrial zone on 24 October, according to the regional governor.

The pressure on Kyiv has been public. On 9 October, Trump announced a deal for Russian diesel, and Treasury suspended sanctions on Russian diesel until April 2027. On 10 October he said, "I think it's time for Ukraine to get a new president," and of the refinery strikes, "He better damn well stop." On 11 October he declared an energy ceasefire that neither Kyiv nor Moscow had announced.

Zelensky's own account differs in scope. On 27 October he told journalists Ukraine had held off on refineries for 72 hours after the truce announcement and that "no one thanked us for those three days." He said Kyiv had offered Washington three alternatives: a mutual energy ceasefire, Starlink access for strikes on Russian ballistic missile launchers, or more Patriot interceptors. None, he said, had been taken up.

The backdrop is commercial as well as military. On 27 October the Financial Times reported that Washington and Moscow have discussed a return of US oil majors to Russia, including a Sakhalin joint venture, Druzhba flows to Europe and a sale of Lukoil's foreign assets. "Nothing is final," a US official told the FT, and Rosneft and Lukoil remain under US sanctions.

The dangerous box is not simply “war or peace.” It is the box labelled coercive diplomacy that may contain an unauthorised offer, an Iranian delaying strategy, proxy action and military preparations moving on separate clocks.

Washington must decide whether Vance is a negotiator or a messenger. 

Tehran must decide whether seven conditions are an opening position or a mechanism for avoiding a decision. Israel’s election weakens Netanyahu’s mandate for discretionary war but gives him an incentive to use Iran to restructure the coalition.

Until those choices become explicit, Iran retains the asymmetric advantage. 

It can impose uncertainty more cheaply than the United States and its allies can remove it. 

Another purely kinetic answer will destroy assets, but it will not end the system that regenerates them.

End Assessment 6/6

text:
BOX RR 
THE HOUTHI VETO

The Houthis believe attacks on Saudi territory, Red Sea shipping and Yemeni government infrastructure prove independence and preserve their relevance to any regional settlement.

Iran believes the same activity supplies leverage without requiring an attributable Iranian strike.

The box may contain loss of control. A missile causing mass casualties at an airport, energy installation or residential area could force Saudi retaliation and collapse the diplomatic channel irrespective of Tehran’s intentions. 

Saudi air cover, Yemeni government ground activity and any Emirati or Saudi special-forces presence also create opportunities for ambush and escalation.

No additional successful Saudi strike has been independently confirmed since the morning reporting period. 

Houthi claims of direct hits should remain separate from verified interceptions, debris and damage.

BOX GG 
THE GULF GUARANTORS

Qatar, Oman, Saudi Arabia and Turkey believe they can provide venues, sequencing and face-saving language. Their leverage is access, not enforcement.

The box may contain a ceasefire that none of the mediators can guarantee. They cannot ensure that Israel will suspend covert action, that the 

Houthis will comply, that Iraqi factions will stand down or that Washington will maintain one negotiating position.

A workable arrangement requires separate verification tracks: nuclear activity, maritime navigation, proxy fires, sanctions relief and Israeli restraint. 

Combining all of them into a single grand bargain makes one spoiler capable of collapsing everything.

BOX RC  
RUSSIA AND CHINA BELOW THE WAR LINE

Moscow and Beijing benefit from an Iran capable of absorbing US attention and consuming Western air-defence interceptors, but neither gains from uncontrolled closure of Hormuz.

Russia’s options include intelligence, diplomatic cover, components and technical support. 

China’s include continued trade, sanctions-resistant finance, dual-use supply chains and pressure for navigation to resume. 

Neither has publicly offered Iran a direct military guarantee.

Their preferred box is prolonged Western expenditure without Russian or Chinese entry into the war. 

The hidden contents are proliferation, greater Iranian dependence and the risk that commercial or intelligence assistance becomes attributable after a mass-casualty attack.

3/6

text:
BERTRAND’S BOX 
ASYMMETRIC ASSESSMENT

29 OCTOBER 2026 
EVENING

STRATEGIC JUDGEMENT

The most consequential change is not a new strike but Washington’s contradictory signalling. 

Tehran confirms receiving Vice President Vance’s letter but has not answered. Reports portrayed it as an invitation to direct negotiations; President Trump subsequently described the contact as concerning medical supplies and denied instructing Vance to restart peace talks. 

This may be deliberate ambiguity: a diplomatic channel disguised as humanitarian contact, preserving deniability if Iran refuses. It may instead expose disagreement or poor coordination inside Washington. 

Either way, Tehran can now question whether any American offer is authoritative. 

US military deterrence remains credible; its diplomatic guarantee does not.

Iran’s advantage remains asymmetric control of time, uncertainty and geography. 

The United States and Israel possess overwhelming conventional striking power, but cannot reliably convert destruction into Iranian compliance. 

Kinetic responses to kinetic actions repeat the same box: each side believes it is restoring deterrence, while the contents are dispersed procurement, proxy retaliation, higher force-protection costs and another strike cycle.

EVIDENCE STATUS

Confirmed:

Tehran acknowledges receipt of the Vance letter and says no response has been delivered.

Trump says the outreach concerned medical supplies, contradicting reports of an authorised peace initiative.

Israel’s completed count gives Netanyahu’s Likud-aligned bloc 53 seats, the Eisenkot-aligned opposition 48 and Arab parties 19. Certification and coalition formation remain ahead; neither main bloc controls 61 seats. 

UKMTO recorded one vessel on fire approximately nine nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman. Its identity and the cause remain undetermined.

CENTCOM rejects the IRGC claim that three tankers struck mines in unauthorised routes and says recognised transit lanes remain open.

Credible but unverified:

The Vance letter proposed a direct meeting, possibly involving a Vance-led delegation and the nuclear issue.

Washington is preparing options for a short, intensive campaign after the US midterm elections. Preparations do not establish a decision to attack.

Three tankers were damaged by mines in Hormuz. Only one vessel fire has been independently recorded; the ships, mines and claimed routing violation remain unverified.

Russia is providing Iran with intelligence derived from space-based collection. 

Correlations between Russian imaging activity and Iranian attacks merit investigation but do not publicly establish tasking or transfer.

ASSESSMENT:

Iran will probably delay its formal response while measuring whether Vance speaks for Trump, whether sanctions relief precedes nuclear discussion and whether US military preparations continue. Delay costs Tehran little and forces Washington to clarify itself first.

THE BOXES

BOX EE 
THE AMERICAN SPLIT SIGNAL

Washington believes it is selecting maximum leverage: military preparations outside the box, a private channel inside it and no public concession.

The box may actually contain a credibility deficit. 

If Trump disowns the diplomatic purpose of Vance’s letter, Iran cannot know whether an agreement negotiated through Vance would survive presidential reversal. 

Tehran can therefore demand a named envoy, written authority and an agreed sequence before making concessions.

Choices:

Clarify that Vance has negotiating authority. This strengthens diplomacy but exposes Trump politically if Iran refuses.

Maintain ambiguity. This preserves deniability but makes substantive Iranian engagement less likely.

Treat silence as rejection and intensify military pressure. 

This strengthens immediate coercion while confirming Tehran’s argument that diplomacy is an ultimatum with better catering.

1/6

text:
🖤🥃🔫 25 MAFIA PERFUMES — THE GODFATHER WARDROBE OF PERFUMERY

Black suits. Leather chairs. Cigar smoke. Whisky glasses. Old money. Cold authority. 🕴️

“Mafia” here isn't simply dark perfume. It means a fragrance with COMMANDING PRESENCE—something that smells mature, expensive, dangerous, confident and impossible to ignore.

1. 🕴️ CHANEL — ANTAEUS

Leather, aromatic herbs, oakmoss, patchouli and animalic warmth. This is old-school DON DNA—dry, masculine, stern and uncompromising.

💥 Performance: Strong opening projection.
⏳ Excellent longevity, particularly older formulations.
🌫️ Creates a serious, masculine trail rather than sugary room-filling diffusion.

2. 💀 YSL — KOUROS
Aromatic freshness crashes into musk, leather, incense and animalic facets. Fearless 1980s masculinity. Nothing shy about it.
💥 Performance: Historically an absolute monster.
⏳ Modern bottles still offer substantial persistence, though vintage is generally fiercer.
🌫️ Easily recognizable musky trail—spray carefully.

3. 🔥 JACQUES BOGART — FURYO

Tobacco, leather, patchouli, woods and animalic darkness. Imagine an 80s gangster stepping from a black Mercedes.

💥 Performance: Powerful old-school construction.
⏳ Long-lasting on skin and considerably longer on clothes.
🌫️ Dark tobacco-leather aura with serious presence.

4. 🚬 DAVIDOFF — ZINO
Lavender, patchouli, sandalwood and vanilla wrapped in barbershop darkness. Mature, smooth and beautifully masculine.
💥 Performance: Moderate-to-strong rather than nuclear today.
⏳ Roughly 6–8 hours is realistic for many wearers.
🌫️ Best feature is its warm, sophisticated scent cloud.

5. 🥃 GUERLAIN — HABIT ROUGE

Citrus brightness over spices, leather, woods, balsams and vanilla. This is not the hitman—this is the educated Godfather.

💥 Performance: Elegant projection rather than brute force.
⏳ Usually good all-round longevity.
🌫️ Beautiful leather-vanilla trail that smells extremely cultured.

6. 🌑 GUERLAIN — BOIS MYSTÉRIEUX
Saffron, cedar, patchouli, leather and myrrh. Dry, smoky and mysterious—a dark palace rendered as perfume.
💥 Performance: Strong first few hours.
⏳ Around 8–10+ hours can be achievable depending on skin.
🌫️ Excellent smoky leather-wood trail, especially in cooler weather.

7. ⛽ DIOR — FAHRENHEIT EDT

Violet leaf, leather, woods and that legendary petrol-like illusion. One spray and everyone knows something entered the room.

💥 Performance: Noticeable projection without becoming ridiculous.
⏳ Generally solid 7–9-hour territory, with batch/skin variation.
🌫️ Its distinctive DNA makes it feel louder than raw projection numbers suggest.

8. 🖤 DIOR — HOMME PARFUM
Dense iris married to leather, ambered woods and darker facets. Powdery but tremendously masculine. The Mafia boss in bespoke tailoring.
💥 Performance: Excellent longevity.
⏳ Often 10+ hours on suitable skin, with clothing holding it much longer.
🌫️ Dense, persistent aura rather than explosive freshness.

9. 🚬 TOM FORD — TOBACCO VANILLE

Tobacco leaf, spices, vanilla, cacao and dried-fruit richness. Private club, mahogany furniture and unlimited money.

💥 Performance: Traditionally one of Tom Ford's stronger performers.
⏳ Excellent longevity—often an all-day fragrance.
🌫️ Rich tobacco-vanilla trail can dominate enclosed spaces.

10. 🌙 TOM FORD — NOIR EXTREME PARFUM
Cardamom, ginger, florals, amber, woods and leather create something dark, smooth and seductive.
💥 Performance: Stronger density than sheer projection suggests.
⏳ Very good longevity, particularly on clothing.
🌫️ Creates a warm, intimate but unmistakably luxurious trail.

11. 😈 TOM FORD — FUCKING FABULOUS

Bitter almond, leather, tonka, woods and aromatic facets. Modern Mafia: provocative, fashionable and slightly arrogant.

💥 Performance: Strong initial presence.
⏳ Good-to-very-good longevity depending on skin.
🌫️ Leather-almond-tonka DNA remains noticeable long after projection settles.

12. 👑 CREED — ABSOLU AVENTUS
Citrus, spices, woods and the darker smoky-fruity Aventus idea. More billionaire kingpin than old-school gangster.
💥 Performance: Strong, attention-grabbing opening.
⏳ Good longevity with a persistent woody drydown.
🌫️ Excellent compliment-style scent trail without becoming oppressive.

13. ☢️ AMOUAGE — INTERLUDE MAN

Oregano, incense, amber, opoponax, leather and oud. THE BLUE BEAST. This is incense warfare.

💥 Performance: MONSTER.
⏳ 12+ hours is entirely plausible, with clothes surviving into the next day.
🌫️ Huge incense-resin cloud—overspraying can overwhelm a room.

14. 👑 AMOUAGE — JUBILATION XXV MAN
Blackberry, frankincense, resins, woods, spices and oud. Regal rather than aggressive—the Don at his private palace.
💥 Performance: Rich and persistent, though batches can vary.
⏳ Generally very good longevity.
🌫️ Sophisticated incense-wood trail; less brutal than Interlude.

15. 🏴 NASOMATTO — BLACK AFGANO

Dark aromatics, smoky woods, resins and coffee-like shadows. Thick, mysterious and instantly recognizable.

💥 Performance: Famous for excellent strength.
⏳ A tiny amount can remain for many hours.
🌫️ Dense smoky-resinous trail—small bottle, enormous personality.

16. 🌋 ORTO PARISI — TERRONI
Earth, smoke, burning woods and dark resinous warmth. Volcanic soil turned into perfume.
💥 Performance: BEAST MODE.
⏳ Easily all-day territory for many wearers.
🌫️ Huge smoky-earthy aura—2–4 sprays can be plenty.

17. 🖤 ORTO PARISI — CUOIUM

Leather pushed into primitive territory—smoke, animalic warmth, woods and darkness. The Mafia enforcer.

💥 Performance: Extremely powerful.
⏳ 10–12+ hours is realistic for many, with clothes lasting far longer.
🌫️ Massive leather trail; absolutely not an office-safe overspray.

18. 🦅 XERJOFF — ALEXANDRIA II
Lavender, cinnamon, rosewood, oud, amber, vanilla and sandalwood. Royal Middle Eastern luxury meets Italian polish.
💥 Performance: Excellent strength.
⏳ Frequently an all-day fragrance.
🌫️ Rich woody-amber trail with excellent diffusion and clothing persistence.

19. 🥃 ROJA — ENIGMA POUR HOMME PARFUM

Cognac character, tobacco, benzoin, vanilla and spices. Millionaire Mafia boss at midnight.

💥 Performance: Deep and persistent rather than screechingly loud.
⏳ Excellent longevity due to its rich parfum structure.
🌫️ Warm cognac-tobacco aura stays beautifully around the wearer.

20. 🌃 ROJA — MANHATTAN
Tobacco, woods, spices, florals and vanilla warmth. Think penthouse, whisky, cigar and tailored cashmere.
💥 Performance: Strong opening and substantial body.
⏳ Very good longevity with excellent clothing persistence.
🌫️ Sophisticated tobacco-spice trail rather than aggressive projection.

21. 🐺 PARFUMS DE MARLY — CARLISLE

Green apple, nutmeg, rose, patchouli and vanilla create a dark sweet-spicy signature. Charismatic and immediately luxurious.

💥 Performance: Very strong.
⏳ Commonly all-day territory on skin.
🌫️ Excellent projection and sillage—easy compliment getter.

22. 🕴️ FRÉDÉRIC MALLE — MONSIEUR.
Patchouli taken almost to its limit, surrounded by rum, incense, cedar and musk. Cold, mature, intimidating sophistication.
💥 Performance: Powerful patchouli presence.
⏳ Excellent longevity—this material clings relentlessly.
🌫️ Dark, earthy trail that announces maturity rather than sweetness.

23. 🐎 MEMO PARIS — AFRICAN LEATHER

Cardamom, saffron, cumin, patchouli, oud and leather. Hot spices over dry leather—luxurious safari-boss energy.

💥 Performance: Strong opening diffusion.
⏳ Very good longevity, usually enough for an evening and beyond.
🌫️ Spicy leather trail remains clearly noticeable for hours.

24. 🍾 PARFUM D’EMPIRE — AMBRE RUSSE
Vodka and Champagne effects collide with cinnamon, tea, leather, incense, musk and amber. Russian oligarch at 2 AM.
💥 Performance: Strong and dense.
⏳ Excellent longevity from its resinous amber foundation.
🌫️ Boozy opening transforms into a smoky amber-leather trail.

25. 💣 BEAUFORT LONDON — IRON DUKE

Leather, gunpowder-like smoke, rum, tobacco and animalic darkness. This doesn't ask permission before entering the room.

💥 Performance: Extremely assertive.
⏳ Long-lasting smoky leather/tobacco character.
🌫️ Serious sillage—keep the spray count controlled indoors.

text:
‼️ BIG NEWS for this 6-year-old boy who was told by doctors he might not survive the summer. He was diagnosed with one of the deadliest childhood brain cancers, with no known cure.

But four months later, his family has shared news they once feared they'd never hear.

HIS BRAIN TUMOR HAS SHRUNK BY 60%!

Many of you may remember Lucas Monreal from El Paso, Texas. I shared his story in June after he was diagnosed with DIPG, an aggressive brain tumor that cannot be surgically removed.

His parents, Alejandra and Luis, were desperately searching for treatment options, hoping to give their little boy more time.

Lucas underwent 28 radiation treatments, and his mom says his symptoms began improving.

Then came the October 19th update confirming the tumor had shrunk by 60%.

Just imagine what that news meant to parents who had been told their son might not make it through the summer.

And now Lucas is in Houston preparing for another important step: an experimental CAR T-cell treatment.

His mom says he'll undergo three days of chemotherapy before the infusion, followed by a hospital stay and weeks of monitoring.

But this fight has taken an enormous toll on the family.

Alejandra, a teacher, has been away from work without regular pay. Luis, an El Paso firefighter, has relied on coworkers covering his shifts. They're also facing medical bills and trying to care for their other children while staying near the hospital.

Thankfully, a firefighters union has provided an apartment for their stay in Houston.

DIPG remains a devastating diagnosis, and tumor shrinkage doesn't mean the cancer is cured.

But Lucas is still here, still fighting, and now has an opportunity to pursue another treatment.

For families facing this terrible disease, I hope his progress offers some encouragement during an incredibly difficult journey.

Please pray that Lucas responds well to CAR T-cell therapy, that his family finds the strength and financial support they need, and that this sweet boy continues defying the odds.

And would you leave Lucas and his family some words of encouragement? They have a long road ahead, but today there's something worth celebrating.

These ideas, gathered up into a single resolution of the Will, can certainly give the Will immense strength. But we must ask: what is it in the soul-life that has been directly attacked? 8 Things You Need to Know about Surveillance
8 important truths about surveillance
ai-in-society
Author
Rachel Thomas

Published
August 7, 2019

Over 225 police departments have partnered with Amazon to have access to Amazon’s video footage obtained as part of the “smart” doorbell product Ring, and in many cases these partnerships are heavily subsidized with taxpayer money. Police departments are allowing Amazon to stream 911 call information directly in real-time, and Amazon requires police departments to read pre-approved scripts when talking about the program. If a homeowner doesn’t want to share data from their video camera doorbell with police, an officer for the Fresno County Sheriff’s Office said they can just go directly to Amazon to obtain it. This creation of an extensive surveillance network, the murky private-public partnership surrounding it, and a lack of any sort of regulations or oversight is frightening. And this is just one of many examples related to surveillance technology that have recently come to light.

I frequently talk with people who are not that concerned about surveillance, or who feel that the positives outweigh the risks. Here, I want to share some important truths about surveillance:

Surveillance can facilitate human rights abuses and even genocide
Data is often used for different purposes than why it was collected
Data often contains errors
Surveillance typically operates with no accountability
Surveillance changes our behavior
Surveillance disproportionately impacts the marginalized
Data privacy is a public good
We don’t have to accept invasive surveillance
While I was writing this post, a number of investigative articles came out with disturbing new developments related to surveillance. I decided that rather than attempt to include everything in one post (which would make it too long and too dense), I would go ahead and share the above facts about surveillance, as they are just a relevant as ever.

Surveillance can facilitate human rights abuses and even genocide
There is a long history of data about sensitive attributes being misused, including the use of the 1940 USA Census to intern Japanese Americans, a system of identity cards introduced by the Belgian colonial government that were later used during the 1994 Rwandan genocide (in which nearly a million people were murdered), and the role of IBM in helping Nazi Germany use punchcard computers to identify and track the mass killing of millions of Jewish people. More recently, the mass internment of over one million people who are part of an ethnic minority in Western China was facilitated through the use of a surveillance network of cameras, biometric data (including images of people’s faces, audio of their voices, and blood samples), and phone monitoring.

Adolf Hitler meeting with IBM CEO Tom Watson Sr. in 1937. Source: Computer History
Pictured above is Adolf Hitler (far left) meeting with IBM CEO Tom Watson Sr. (2nd from left), shortly before Hitler awarded Watson a special “Service to the Reich” medal in 1937 (for a timeline of the Holocaust, see here). Watson returned the medal in 1940, although IBM continued to do business with the Nazis. IBM technology helped the Nazis conduct detailed censuses in countries they occupied, to thoroughly identify anyone of Jewish descent. Nazi concentration camps used IBM’s punchcard machines to tabulate prisoners, recording whether they were Jewish, gay, or Gypsies, and whether they died of “natural causes,” execution, suicide, or via “special treatment” in gas chambers. It is not the case that IBM sold the machines and then was done with it. Rather, IBM and its subsidiaries provided regular training and maintenance on-site at the concentration camps: printing off cards, configuring machines, and repairing them as they broke frequently.

Data is often used for different purposes than why it was collected
In the above examples, the data collection began before genocide was committed. IBM began selling to Nazi Germany well before the Holocaust (although continued for far too long), including helping with Germany’s 1933 census conducted by Adolf Hitler, which was effective at identifying far more Jewish people than had previously been recognized in Germany.

It is important to recognize how data and images gathered through surveillance can be weaponized later. Columbia professor Tim Wu wrote that “One [hard truth] is that data and surveillance networks created for one purpose can and will be used for others. You must assume that any personal data that Facebook or Android keeps are data that governments around the world will try to get or that thieves will try to steal.”

#CarnivalLuminosa to Debut from #Baltimore Following Refresh, Joining Carnival Miracle to Expand Cruise Offerings

MIAMI, Oct. 29, 2026 – Carnival Cruise Line today opened sailings for its 2028/29 schedule from Baltimore, offering one of Carnival's most diverse cruise programs and featuring a wide range of voyages aboard Carnival Luminosa and Carnival Miracle to The Bahamas, Bermuda, Canada and the Caribbean.

Beginning in November 2028, Carnival Luminosa will make her Baltimore debut fresh from dry dock with refreshed spaces and enhancements throughout the ship. The ship will join #CarnivalMiracle in Baltimore, giving guests more options to sail from the Mid-Atlantic with itineraries now available through April 2029 and ranging from 6 to 14 days.

From Bermuda’s pink-sand beaches and the fall colors of the Atlantic Canada to the turquoise waters of the Caribbean, Carnival Luminosa and Carnival Miracle will connect Baltimore to 22 unforgettable destinations. 

The wide-ranging itineraries include visits to Paradise Collection destinations Celebration Key in Grand Bahama, RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay, Grand Turk and Amber Cove.
Carnival Luminosa will offer a range of seven- to 14-day itineraries, giving guests even more ways to explore from Baltimore. Seven- and eight-day cruises will visit The Bahamas, while nine-day sailings will cruise to the Eastern Caribbean. For guests looking to venture farther, 12- and 14-day Carnival Journeys voyages will sail deep into the Southern Caribbean, with visits to Aruba, Curaçao, Barbados, Martinique, St. Kitts, St. Lucia, St. Croix, St. Maarten and St. Thomas.

New sailings now open on Carnival Miracle will extend from September 2028-April 2029 with a mix of Bahamas, Bermuda, Canada/New England, Southern Caribbean and Eastern Caribbean cruises. Guests can choose from six- to eight-day sailings to The Bahamas and Bermuda, along with nine-day Eastern Caribbean cruises to Amber Cove, San Juan and St. Maarten or St. Thomas. For a more immersive itinerary, eight Carnival Journeys voyages of 12 to 14 days explore the Eastern and the Southern Caribbean, visiting destinations such as Antigua, Aruba, Barbados, Bonaire, Curacao, Dominica, Martinique, St. Lucia, St. Kitts and Tortola. 

The ship will also operate two eight-day Canada/New England cruises in September 2028, visiting destinations including Portland, Maine; Halifax, Nova Scotia and Saint John, New Brunswick.
